exposure: Delivery mode (Caesarean section vs. vaginal birth)
outcome: Levels of lipokines in human milk
Levels of 5-palmitic acid ester of hydroxystearic acid (5-PAHSA)
cohort: Mothers who delivered via caesarean section or vaginal birth, and delivered preterm or at term
finding: Mothers delivering term babies vaginally produce colostrum with higher levels of 5-PAHSA, potentially contributing to the prevention of intestinal inflammation in newborns.
mod_finding: Caesarean section negatively affected colostrum lipidome, including 5-PAHSA levels, compared to vaginal birth, but the lipidomic profiles normalized in mature milk.
